purpose: Resolve the material objective-and-training uncertainty before spending a scarce experiment on the highest-priority unexplored direction: a ranking-aligned loss. The current seed uses pointwise logistic training, while fixed research context prioritizes pairwise/listwise alternatives; implementation details are needed to define a leakage-safe, computationally bounded single-loss ablation.
query: Within-user implicit-feedback recommendation with binary long-view labels: practical pairwise ranking objectives (RankNet/BPR) versus pointwise logistic loss, including pair construction within user impression groups, negative sampling, and effects on GAUC and top-k nDCG.

purpose: Resolve whether a causal history representation can be implemented safely and efficiently with the available impression logs after the screened aggregate affinity features were rejected. Literature is needed to distinguish a candidate-aware sequence mechanism from the already rejected coarse historical aggregates and to establish appropriate temporal truncation and cold-user defaults.
query: Causally truncated user behavior history models for candidate ranking in short-video recommendation: candidate-conditioned attention or compact sequence pooling, impression-time feature construction, cold-user handling, and efficient training/evaluation under temporal splits.
